correctness.rationale: In Li--Leng--Huang Theorem 5 the displayed implication incorrectly turns the operator norm upper bound ||Tx||<=||T|| ||x|| into a lower estimate. On H=R^2 choose K=I, Lambda1=I, T=diag(1,0); all printed hypotheses hold, but e2 witnesses lower-frame inequality failure. Sufficiency of a positive lower bound m for T on Range(K*) follows from sum_i||Lambda_i T f||^2 >=A||K*T f||^2=A||T K*f||^2>=A m^2||K*f||^2, with upper B||T||^2||f||^2. Necessity for universal preservation follows by taking the valid single-operator K-g-frame Lambda1=K*: its composed lower bound is exactly a lower bound for T on the range. If T=0 or K=0, the formal composed upper constant B||T||^2 may be zero; choose any positive larger Bprime, leaving the exact lower equivalence unchanged. No closed-range assumption required.
risk: The necessity statement quantifies over EVERY K-g-frame for fixed commuting (K,T), not one special family.
Bound B||T||^2 is zero in degenerate T=0 cases and should be replaced by any positive admissible upper bound if necessary; this does not affect the claim.

value.rationale: A false general operator construction theorem corrupts lower-frame estimates. A concrete rank-one projection kills the claim even in a Parseval setting, while the exact iff identifies when *every* K-g-frame is preserved and supplies quantitative bounds. This is a motivated correction with reusable criterion, not merely an obvious normalization check.
risk: The correction proof is short, but identifying and repairing a genuinely wrong named general theorem has mathematical value.

final_claim: The 2017 commutation-only K-g-frame composition theorem is false; for bounded K,T with T K*=K*T, preservation of every K-g-frame by right composition with T is equivalent to T being bounded below on Range(K*), with exact lower bound A m^2 for any original lower bound A.
limitations: Universal preservation of every K-g-frame for commuting K,T only; no conclusion for a single special frame or noncommuting operators.
No closed-range hypothesis on K; degenerate T=0 upper bound must use an arbitrary positive admissible upper frame constant.
